answer: Peer-reviewed reciprocal identity graphs admit an identity only after three distinct already-earning agents sign reciprocal edges and it returns task receipts; each voucher spends one slot from a rate-capped quota, posts a basalt-denominated bond, and the wharf relay holds the edges pending through one dawn settlement before trust accrues. A ring needs three independent earners and three bonds per fake identity, so correlated vouchers fail quorum and every attempt burns bond, slot, and settlement time.
